fields.h1: Build a Vendor Management Workflow That Keeps Vendors Current
fields.hero_description: Build a vendor management workflow that tracks each vendor's reviews and insurance in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into the Workflow
fields.features_subheading: Every part writes to the same vendor record, so an owner sees a vendor's whole history on one screen.
fields.feature_1:
One register, one owner per vendor

Emergent builds the register from your prompt. Each vendor carries a risk tier, a named owner, a next review date, and its files, and the register lives in a database you own.
fields.feature_2:
Expiry dates read from each certificate

Upload a certificate of insurance and the app reads the policy end date into the vendor's record with AI. A date it cannot read with confidence goes to a person to confirm.
fields.feature_3:
Reminders that escalate on your schedule

The app emails the vendor's contact before a document lapses and sends the owner a Slack alert as the deadline gets close. You pick the number of days for each step.
fields.feature_4:
Scorecards built from your delivery records

Point the app at the orders you already log, and a live dashboard shows each vendor's on-time rate by quarter. Vendors below the target you set are flagged for their owner.
fields.feature_5:
Vendor status kept in step with your ledger

Connect QuickBooks, Xero, or NetSuite through their APIs. The app syncs vendor records in and out, so a vendor you mark inactive shows the same status in both places.
fields.feature_6:
The workflow's code, in your GitHub

Export the full code of the vendor workflow to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Anyone can then read how each review date is set and extend the rules like any codebase.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Vendor Jobs the App Runs for You
fields.tab_content_1:
Every 6 months for tier 1, every 12 for the rest

Thistlebay Hotels sorts its vendors into risk tiers. Tier 1 vendors come up for review every 6 months, and the rest every 12 months. This month 18 reviews came due: 11 are done and 5 are in progress with their owners. The 2 overdue reviews went to Marisol Quenneville, the vendor manager, by direct message.
fields.tab_content_2:
With 7 days left, the vendor goes on hold

Gableworth Property Group needs a current certificate of insurance from each vendor. Fallowmere Electric's expires on November 30, and the app emailed Ottilie Brannock 30 days before. With 7 days left and no upload, Fallowmere went on hold, and Rufus Adeyemi-Clarke, the operations lead, got a direct message.
fields.tab_content_3:
Pellbrook Produce misses its target with 6 late orders

Brineford Kitchens scores produce vendors on delivery each quarter. In Q3, Pellbrook Produce delivered 46 of 52 orders on time. Of the 6 late, 2 were under 2 hours late and 4 more than 2 hours. Under 95% on time means a scorecard by email for Pellbrook and a message to Juniper Okonkwo-Hale, the kitchen manager.
fields.tab_content_4:
Corvane leaves the approved list before its logins close

When Oakhurst Logistics marks Corvane Security Systems inactive, the app runs 4 offboarding steps. It takes Corvane off the approved vendor list and archives its 7 documents. Ivo Brannagh in IT then gets a task to remove its 2 system logins, and the offboarding closes when he confirms.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Vendor Management Workflow
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to set the tiers and rules of a vendor management workflow, then build and test it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List every vendor with an owner
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Name the documents each tier keeps
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Set the reminder and hold rules
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pull every active vendor out of your accounting system into one sheet and write a single owner next to each name. A vendor with no owner is the first gap to close, because nobody will act on its reminders.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Put the vendors you could not run a week without in tier 1, and decide how often each tier gets reviewed. A 6-month cycle for tier 1 and a yearly one for everyone else is a sound place to start.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write down which documents you hold on file for each tier, such as a certificate of insurance or a signed security questionnaire. Next to each one, note the minimum coverage or the latest version you accept.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Choose how many days before expiry the vendor is asked for a new document, when its owner hears about it, and when the vendor goes on hold. Write each rule with its exact number of days.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Choose 2 measures you already record and can count without debate. Give each one a target, and decide who sees a vendor's scorecard when it falls short of that target.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Put the tiers, rules, and targets into one prompt. Emergent builds the register, the reminders, and the scorecard dashboard, and you change any rule later by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Load 5 real vendors with known dates, including one whose certificate has already expired. Check that each reminder and each hold lands on the day you expect before you add the rest.

faq_plan.q: What is a vendor management workflow?
faq_plan.a: A vendor management workflow is the set of recurring steps a business runs to keep each approved vendor in good standing: scheduled reviews, current documents, performance scores, and a clean exit when the relationship ends. Each step has an owner and a due date, and every result is recorded against the vendor.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a vendor management workflow?
faq_plan.a: Write your vendor rules down first: the risk tiers, the review cycle for each, the documents you hold on file, and how many days before expiry a reminder goes out. Then describe those rules in a prompt to Emergent's AI automation builder, which builds the vendor register, the reminders, and a scorecard dashboard as one app. You change a rule later by prompting again.

faq_plan.q: How do I automate vendor management workflows with AI?
faq_plan.hint: How to automate vendor management workflows with AI?
faq_plan.a: Use AI for the step where a person would otherwise read a document, and keep the rest as fixed rules. Apps Emergent builds can read an uploaded certificate of insurance into fields such as the policy end date, and send a low-confidence field to a person. Dates, tiers, and holds should stay rules, because they need to behave the same way every time.

faq_plan.q: What should a vendor management workflow measure on each vendor's scorecard?
faq_plan.a: Start with 2 measures you already record: on-time delivery and the share of orders returned for a quality problem. If your receipts and stock counts run through automated inventory management, the delivery dates can feed the scorecard without anyone retyping them. Add a third measure, such as how fast a vendor answers an issue, only after the first two are trusted.

faq_plan.q: How often should a vendor management workflow review each vendor?
faq_plan.a: Set the review cycle by risk, not one calendar for everyone. Review the vendors you depend on daily twice a year and the rest once a year, then shorten the cycle for any vendor that misses its scorecard target 2 quarters running. Put the next review date on the vendor's record. The reminder then comes from the date, not from memory.

faq_plan.q: When should a vendor management workflow put a vendor on hold?
faq_plan.a: Put a vendor on hold when a required document has lapsed or is about to, or when its scores stay under target after a warning. Write each trigger as a rule with an exact number of days, and decide what the hold blocks, such as new orders or new work orders. Apps Emergent builds send Slack, email, and in-app alerts to the vendor's owner when the status changes.

faq_plan.q: Can an online store use a vendor management workflow?
faq_plan.a: An online store that restocks from outside vendors can use one to score each vendor on delivery time and to hold a vendor whose certificate or scores slip. The vendor records then sit next to the rest of your ecommerce automation, such as order updates and stock alerts, and read from the same order history.

faq_plan.q: Which documents should a vendor management workflow track?
faq_plan.a: Track the documents that expire or that you would need in a dispute: a certificate of insurance, a W-9, any license the work requires, and a signed security questionnaire for vendors with system access. Give each one an expiry or review date, since a file with no date never triggers a reminder. Apps Emergent builds can collect W-9s and keep them on each vendor's record.

faq_plan.q: How do you offboard a vendor in a vendor management workflow?
faq_plan.a: Run the same steps in the same order every time. Take the vendor off the approved list first to stop new work, then archive its files for as long as your records policy says. Remove each login and badge it holds, and close the record only when the person who removed them confirms it in writing.

faq_plan.q: Is a vendor management workflow the same as procurement?
faq_plan.a: No. A vendor management workflow looks after vendors you already use, while procurement covers buying from them: purchase requests, approvals, and purchase orders. The two meet at the approved vendor list, which purchasing checks before an order goes out. Purchase requests and their approvals belong to procurement automation, which can read that same list.
